We're seeing a sustained 5xx spike and tail latency (p95/p99) across our dedicated pool (pool-phi-03) starting ~08:45 PDT. Error rate jumped to ~3.7% (baseline ~0.02%) and avg token throughput has fallen ~40%. This is impacting our checkout microservice (sync calls to Redwood generation).

Quick facts:
- Affected region: us-west (pool-phi-03, reserved capacity for PulseCommerce)
- Symptom: 503/504 and a bunch of long-running responses (5–20s)
- User impact: intermittent checkout failures for ~8% of sessions in the last 30m

Attached are logs and a short timeline (ops-logs-0707.tar.gz). We're on a customer-facing incident call now — can Redwood ops weigh in on whether this is a noisy-tenant issue, or capacity starvation? We need a mitigation plan in the next 30–60 minutes.

Thanks,

Subject: RE: Production: 5xx spike + tail latency on our dedicated pool (pool-phi-03) — triage update

Quick triage (summary):

- Root signal: high eviction/IO pressure on KV cache for pool-phi-03. We see a small number of tenants exhibiting very high prefix reuse, driving the cache to thrash and causing long tail times during KV load misses.
- Impact metrics: 5xx rate ~3.7% (peak 4.1% at 09:05), p95 latency 8.6s, p99 latency 18.3s. Token throughput reduced ~38% on average for the pool.
- Hot-tenant: tenant ID T-6721 accounts for ~55% of the read/write rate on that pool (noisy neighbor).

Short-term mitigations we've validated and can apply immediately (recommended order):
1) Tenant isolation: move T-6721 to a separate shard within the pool (fast but will require brief connections drain ~30–60s).
2) Soft-fallback routing: route PulseCommerce requests to their quantized model variant (q4) for up to 2 hours — reduces memory pressure and latency at cost of ~3–5% quality degradation.
3) Rate-limits: apply soft throttling to top 5% of sessions for T-6721 (limits tail usage without full service interruption).

Estimated effect: isolation + soft-fallback should reduce 5xx below 0.1% and restore >85% throughput within 20–40 minutes. If isolation isn't viable (stateful sessions blocking), then the fastest path is an authorized burst to double the available GPU headroom for 4–6 hours.

Attachments: pool-heap-sample-20270707.json (heap snapshot), pool-usage-0707.csv (one-hour resolution pool metrics)

I'll implement tenant isolation first if Ops approves; otherwise will enable fallback routing.

—Olga
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Escalation: PulseCommerce dedicated pool disruption — ask for burst & customer remediation approval

Team —

Update: Olga's isolation steps + soft-fallback routing were applied at ~14:05 and we saw partial recovery. 5xx rate reduced to ~0.4% and throughput recovered to ~78% of baseline, but we still observe intermittent tail spikes tied to background KV rebuilds. The customer's traffic pattern (T-6721) is very bursty and will re-trigger pressure during their peak tonight.

We need a short, timeboxed exec decision to avoid repeat outages and preserve the relationship. Proposed asks (please respond with APPROVE / DENY by 18:00 PDT today):

1) Burst authorization — short-term reserved headroom:
   - Scope: increase PulseCommerce reserved GPUs from current capacity to +120 GPUs (effectively double headroom) across us-west for up to 6 hours (one-time).
   - Expected cost (rough): ~$28,000 (one-time).
   - Expected benefit: immediate elimination of KV pressure and normalization of token throughput to >95% baseline while we enact long-term partitioning.

2) Customer remediation — one-time credit:
   - Offer: 25% credit on July invoice tied to SLA deviation; allows customer to accept soft-fallback without churn risk.

3) Routing priority change (temporary):
   - Authorize Redwood routing to prefer dedicated fallback variant for heavy prefix sessions during customer's peak window today (20:00–22:00 PDT).

If we get approvals, Olga will schedule the burst (infrastructure ops) and Jordan/Marissa will finalize the customer comms (we'll say we're offering fallback + credit + immediate headroom). If DENY, we'll proceed with only soft-fallback and rate-limits but expect residual degradation and higher chance of repeat incidents.

Attachments: draft-burst-authorization.pdf (cost estimate + steps), link to incident doc: https://drive.google.com/incident/pulsecommerce-20270707

Suggested succinct reply: APPROVE BURST + CREDIT (or DENY).

Jonas Weber
